prompt: Draw the graph of a linear function f(x) such that the line passes through the points (0,3) and (3,0), but at x=2, the point (2,1) is not included on the line (use an open circle at (2,1)), and instead, the point (2,2) is included (use a solid dot at (2,2)).

Draw a circle with center O and radius 5. Draw diameter AC. Draw a chord BD perpendicular to AC such that it intersects AC at point E, with CE = 2. Mark all points (A, B, C, D, E, O), and indicate the right angle at E where BD is perpendicular to AC. Label the lengths OA=5, OD= 5 and CE = 2.

Draw a circle labeled O with two intersecting chords AB and CD meeting at point E inside the circle. Mark points A, B, C, and D on the circumference such that chord AB and chord CD intersect at E. Draw a triangle ABC inscribed in a circle with center P. From P, draw perpendiculars to each side of the triangle, and label the distances from P to sides BC, AC, and AB as 6, 4, and 2 units, respectively. Indicate all right angles at the feet of the perpendiculars.

Draw a triangle ABC with an inscribed circle (incircle) centered at O, such that the circle is tangent to sides AB, BC, and AC at points F, E, and D respectively. Mark the points of tangency F on AB, E on BC, and D on AC.

Draw a triangle ABC circumscribed about a circle O (incircle), such that the circle is tangent to sides AB, BC, and CA at points E, F, and D respectively. Clearly label all points (A, B, C, D, E, F, O) and ensure the incircle is tangent to each side at the specified points.

Draw an isosceles triangle ABC with AC = AB = 12, and base BC. Inscribe a circle inside the triangle, and let O be the center of the incircle. Draw a segment AP passing through O such that P is the point where the incircle is tangent to BC. Label all relevant points (A, B, C, O, P).

Draw a geometric diagram showing two circles of radius 5 that are externally tangent to each other and both internally tangent to a larger circle of radius 13. Clearly indicate the points of tangency between each small circle and the large circle, labeling them as A and B.

A circle with a radius of 5 units is divided into 24 congruent sectors. Draw a geometric diagram where N congruent semicircles are placed along the diameter of a larger semicircle, such that the diameters of the small semicircles exactly cover the diameter of the large semicircle without overlap. Plot the graph of the function y = log_{10}(2x + 3) for x in the interval [-5, 5]. Clearly indicate the vertical asymptote, the zero of the function, and the maximum value within the given interval. Mark the coordinates of the zero and the maximum value on the graph.

Draw a geometric diagram showing two circles labeled X and Y, with an external point T. On a Cartesian coordinate plane, draw a circle centered at (-1, -4) with a radius of 3, a line segment connecting the points (-8, -4) and (-9, 2), and a point at (-3, 2). Clearly mark and label all coordinates as specified.

Draw a right triangle ABC with right angle at B, where AB = 20 units and BC = 21 units. Clearly label the vertices A, B, and C. Draw the hypotenuse AC, and mark a point P on AC. Draw a geometric diagram where points A, B, and C are collinear and vertical, with A at the top, B below A, and C at the bottom. From point D to the right of C, draw segments AD and BD. Draw a three-dimensional diagram showing a sphere and a cylinder, each with at least one tangent plane touching their surfaces. For both the sphere and the cylinder, indicate the normal vector at the point of tangency, and clearly label the tangent planes and normals.

Draw a regular tetrahedron labeled with vertices A, B, C, and D. Mark the midpoint M of edge AB. Highlight and color the line segments CM and MD in red. Ensure all vertices are labeled, and the geometric relationships (regularity, midpoint) are visually clear.

Draw a quadrilateral network ABCD with diagonals intersecting at a point, and label the six interior angles at the vertices and intersection as θ₁, θ₂, θ₃, θ₄, θ₅, and θ₆, such that θ₁ is at vertex A, θ₂ and θ₃ are at vertex B, θ₄ and θ₅ are at vertex D, and θ₆ is at vertex C. The diagonals should cross inside the quadrilateral, forming two triangles sharing the intersection point.

Draw a convex quadrilateral ABCD such that its diagonals AC and BD intersect at their midpoints, and mark all interior angles at each vertex as follows: at vertex A, two adjacent angles of 60° and 58°; at vertex B, two adjacent angles of 30° and 35°; at vertex C, two adjacent angles of 55° and 65°; at vertex D, two adjacent angles of 32° and 25°. Indicate all angle measures with proper arc notations.

Draw a diagram of a braced quadrilateral (a four-sided polygon with a diagonal brace connecting two non-adjacent vertices), and label the eight internal angles formed at the vertices and intersections of the brace as θ₁, θ₂, θ₃, θ₄, θ₅, θ₆, θ₇, and θ₈, such that each angle is clearly associated with its respective position in the figure.

A square with side length 1 is labeled with vertices A, B, C, and D in order. The square is folded so that vertex C lands on edge AD at a point labeled C'. Draw the resulting figure, clearly marking points A, B, C, D, and C', and indicate the intersection point E of edges BC and AB after the fold.

Draw a rectangle with side lengths 4 and 8, and inscribe a square of side length 5 such that three of its vertices lie on three different sides of the rectangle. Shade the region that is inside both the square and the rectangle.

On a Cartesian plane with arrowed x- and y-axes and the origin O, illustrate the optimization setup: plot the arch of y = cos x for x in [-π/2, π/2]. Inscribe a rectangle whose base lies on the x-axis and whose two upper vertices lie on the cosine curve at x = ±a. Draw vertical sides at x = −a and x = +a and a horizontal top at height y = cos a. Mark the right upper vertex as (x, y).

Given a square ABCD, draw point E such that it lies outside the square on the extension of the side CD, forming an angle CDE = 110° on the side opposite to A with respect to line CD. Then, locate point F on segment AD such that DE = DF. Draw and label all relevant points, lines, and the 110° angle at D.

In a square ABCD, let P be a point on side AD and Q be a point on side AB. Draw segments BP and CQ such that they intersect at point R inside the square, forming a right angle at R. Mark the lengths BR = 6 and PR = 7. Clearly label all vertices, points P, Q, and R, and indicate the right angle at R. Do not include any additional information or calculations.

Draw a diagram of a baseball diamond represented as a square with each side measuring 90 feet. Label the four vertices as Home plate (H), First base (I), Second base (II), and Third base (III). Draw and label the following: (1) a dashed line from H to II, (2) a line from H to a point R on the segment from II to III, (3) label the distance from II to R as x, the distance from H to R as u.

Draw a simple polygon with vertices labeled A, B, C, D, E, and F in order, such that all interior angles are right angles. The side BC has length 12 units, CD has length 5 units, and EF has length 3 units. Label all vertices and the given side lengths on the diagram.

Draw a simple polygon with vertices labeled A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H in order, such that all interior angles are right angles (90 degrees). The segment AB is 10 units, BC is 8 units, DE is 3 units, and GH is 2 units. Label all vertices and mark the given side lengths on the corresponding segments.

Draw a regular hexagon labeled $ABCDEF$ with side length 2. Mark $G$ as the midpoint of $\\overline{AB}$ and $H$ as the midpoint of $\\overline{DE}$. Highlight the quadrilateral $GCHF$ formed by connecting points $G$, $C$, $H$, and $F$ inside the hexagon.
Draw a trapezoid ABCD such that angles at vertices D and A are right angles, AB = BC, and angle ABC is 120 degrees. Mark the vertices in order (A, B, C, D) and ensure that AC = 12 units.

Geometry construction task: Draw an isosceles trapezoid ABCD with AB parallel to CD and AB > CD. Place A at the bottom-left, B at the bottom-right, D at the top-left, and C at the top-right so that AB is the lower base and CD the upper base. Add an interior point and connect it to points A, B, C, and D with line segments. These four segments must partition the trapezoid into four triangles whose areas, starting from the triangle adjacent to base CD and proceeding clockwise, are in the ratios 2:3:4:5 (i.e., smallest at the top near CD, then right, then left, then largest at the bottom). Label the vertices A, B, C, D; annotate each region with its area.
On the same set of axes, plot the graphs of y = sin(x) and y = -sin(x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. Shade the region bounded between these two curves over this interval.

Draw a geometric diagram showing point B as the vertex, with five rays extending from B labeled such that three of them terminate at points A, C, and two others at D and E. Mark and label five adjacent angles at B as L1, L2, L3, L4, and L5, with L1 between BA and the next ray, L2 between that ray and BC, L3 between BC and the next ray, L4 between BA and the next ray, and L5 between that ray and the last ray. Ensure that points A, B, and C are marked with triangle symbols.

Given triangle ABC, use a compass to construct points D and E on sides AB and AC, respectively, such that both are equidistant from vertex A. Then, using a compass, construct point F such that it is equidistant from D and E. Draw the ray AF, and mark its intersection G with side BC. Illustrate all compass arcs used in the construction.

Draw a geometric diagram showing two parallel lines AB and CD, both intersected by a transversal line EF. Mark the intersection points as O (on AB) and the intersection with CD such that angle 1, formed between EF and CD. Clearly label all points (A, B, C, D, E, F, O) and indicate angle 1 at the intersection of EF and CD.

Draw a parallelogram ABCD where angle B is 60 degrees. Construct the angle bisector of angle BAD, and let it intersect BC at point E. Draw lines AE and DE. Clearly indicate all points and label them appropriately.

Draw a rhombus ABCD with diagonals AC and BD intersecting at point O. Mark a point H on side AB such that DH is perpendicular to AB. Draw segments DH and DO. Clearly label all points A, B, C, D, O, and H.

Draw a parallelogram ABCD. Mark E as the midpoint of side AB, and F as a point on side AD such that AF:FD = 1:2. Draw line segment EF, and let it intersect diagonal AC at point G. Clearly label all points (A, B, C, D, E, F, G).

Draw two triangles sharing the side BC: Triangle ABC is a right triangle with AB = 12.0, BC = 18.0, and angle ACB = 30°. Triangle CBD is an isosceles triangle with CB as its base, angle DBC = 60°, and sides BD = DC. Clearly label all given side lengths and angles.

Construct a geometric diagram as follows: Draw an isosceles right triangle ABC with AB = BC = 9 units and angle ABC = 45°. Attach a square CBDE to side CB such that CB is one side of the square. Then, attach another square DEFG to side DE of the first square, so that DE is a side of both squares. Inscribe a circle inside square DEFG. Mark all right angles and label all points. Indicate the given lengths and the 45° angle.

Construct a geometric diagram consisting of a right triangle ABC with AB = 10.0 units, BC = 13.0 units, and angle ABC = 90°. Attach a parallelogram CBDE to side BC such that angle DBC = 45°. Clearly label all vertices and indicate the given side lengths and angles.

Draw a geometric diagram consisting of a right triangle ABC with a right angle at B, where AB = 11.0 units and BC = 8.0 units. Angle BCA is 60°. Below BC, construct a square CBDE such that BC is one side of the square. Inscribe a circle inside the square. Clearly label all points (A, B, C, D, E) and indicate the right angles and the 60° angle at C.

Plot the graph of the function y = 3*sin(2x + 6) for x in the interval [-π, π]. Mark and label the local maxima, local minima, and all zeros of the function within this interval, showing their coordinates to two decimal places.

Construct a circle with center O and diameter AB. Draw a chord CD perpendicular to AB at point H. Through A, draw a line AP parallel to CO, intersecting the tangent to the circle at D at point E, intersecting BD at point P, and intersecting CD at point F. From E, draw GE perpendicular to CD, meeting the extension of CD at G. Label all points and indicate right angles where appropriate.

Given a rectangle ABCD with AB = 4 and AD = 3, draw its diagonal AC. Let point E be a variable point on the polyline BCD. Construct the reflection F of E across AC. Construct the reflection G of B across AC. Draw lines EG, CG, and BF. Mark the intersection O of BG and AC, and the intersection H of BG and CD. Clearly label all points (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, O, H) and use dashed lines for auxiliary constructions.

In the right triangle ABC with angle ABC = 90° and angle BAC = 60°, let D be a point on AC. Rotate segment CD about point C clockwise by 30° to obtain segment CE. Connect DE and let P be the midpoint of DE. Connect BP. Then, connect CP and construct BP' perpendicular to CP, with P' lying on the extension of CP. Through D', draw D'G perpendicular to AB at point G. Draw the complete geometric figure with all these constructions and label all points as described.

Given a right triangle ABC with \\( \\angle BCA = 90^\\circ \\) and AB as the base. Construct points D and E on AB so that AD < DE < EB, and draw perpendiculars from D to AC (meeting at Q) and from E to BC (meeting at F). Shade the regions of ACD, CDEF and EFB, labeled I, II, and III. Clearly mark all points.

Construct a geometric figure as follows: Draw a circle with diameter AB = 8, and let O be its center. Draw a tangent AE at point A, with AE = 2√7. Construct rhombus ACDE with AE as one side and C lying on the circle. Let CD intersect AB at F. Connect CE and extend it to meet the circle again at G. Connect GF. Draw OC, BG, and AG. Draw CI perpendicular to EA, meeting the extension of EA at I. Draw GH perpendicular to EA at H, and extend GH to meet the extension of CD at J. Label all points.

Construct a right triangle ABC with angle B = 90°, AB = 4 units, and BC = 3 units. Reflect triangle ABC over AC to obtain triangle AB'C. Then reflect triangle AB'C over AB' to obtain triangle AB'C'. Draw a line through C parallel to AB, intersecting AC' at D. From A, draw AE perpendicular to CD, meeting at E. From C', draw C'G perpendicular to AE. Label all points as shown.

Construct a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD inscribed in circle O such that angle BAD = 90°, and the arc length of AB is half that of CD. Let E be the midpoint of BC. Draw lines BD, AE (extend AE), and mark their intersection as F. Extend AE to meet the circle again at G. Given that tan(angle CBD) = 3/4 and AB = sqrt(10), construct point J on the circle such that arc AJ = arc AB. Extend BA to meet the extension of DJ at I. Draw the diameter AH through A. Label all points and lines accordingly.

In a rectangle ABCD, draw a circle centered at vertex A. Let the circle be tangent to diagonal BD at point E. From vertex C, draw a tangent CG to the circle, with G as the point of tangency. Let CG be perpendicular to BD at point F. Connect AE, AG, and AC. Clearly label all points A, B, C, D, E, F, and G.

Given triangle ABC, let point M be on segment BC such that MC = 2MB. Connect AM, and let N be the midpoint of AM. Connect CN and extend it to meet AB at point D. On CN, mark point G such that NC = 3GC. Draw all relevant segments and label all points (A, B, C, M, N, D, G) clearly.

On a Cartesian coordinate plane, draw two circles: one centered at (2, 3) with a radius of 1, and another centered at (5, -4) with a radius of 2. Additionally, draw a sector with its center at (3, 5) and a radius of 1. Use different colors to distinguish the two circles, and clearly mark the centers of all three shapes with their coordinates.

Given a circle with center O and radius 2√3, draw its diameter AB. Let C be the midpoint of OB. Through C, draw a line perpendicular to OB, intersecting the circle at points D and E. Let F be a point on the circle. Connect FD. Through A, draw a line perpendicular to AB, extending to meet the extension of FD at point H, such that DH = 3√7. From D, draw DG perpendicular to AH at G. From F, draw FQ perpendicular to DE, meeting DE at M. From O, draw OQ perpendicular to FQ, with the two lines intersecting at Q. Label all points.

In rectangle ABCD with AB = 6 and AD = 8, let E be a variable point on side CD. Draw BG perpendicular to AE at point G, and extend CG to meet AD at point F. Let O be the center of the rectangle. Draw and label the segments OF, OG, and OC. Clearly indicate all points and auxiliary lines.

Draw a circle with center O. From a point P outside the circle, draw a tangent PA to the circle at point A, and a secant PBC passing through points B and C on the circle. Mark the lengths PA = 8 and PB = 4. Clearly label all points (P, A, B, C, O) and indicate the tangent and secant lines.

Draw a circle labeled O with points A, B, C, and D on its circumference such that chords AB and CD intersect at point E inside the circle. From an external point F, draw a secant passing through points D, A, and extending to F, and a tangent from F touching the circle at B. Also, draw chord AC. Label all points (A, B, C, D, E, F, O).

Draw a circle with center A. On the circumference, mark five distinct points labeled C, D, E, F, such that chords CD and EF intersect at a point G inside the circle. Draw all of the following chords: CD, EF, CE, and FD. Clearly label all points (A, C, D, E, F, G).

Draw a circle with center O. From a point A outside the circle, draw two secants: one secant passes through points D and B on the circle, and the other passes through points E, O, and C, with E between A and O. Mark the following lengths: AE = 4, AB = 12, and DB = 6. Label all points (A, B, C, D, E, O) clearly.

Draw a circle with a diameter of 300 feet. Inside the circle, draw a chord that is also the diameter, and from the midpoint of this diameter, construct an equilateral triangle with a base of 150 feet and an apex angle of 60°, such that the triangle is inscribed below the diameter. Label all relevant lengths and angles.

Draw a circle with center O. Inside the circle, draw two intersecting chords AB and CD such that they intersect at point E inside the circle. Label the points A, B, C, D, E, and O. Ensure that the intersection point E is not at the center. The diagram should clearly show the two chords crossing at E.
